units.en: This is the so-called "Yangzhou smashes — Wuxing overturns pots"; pots are earthenware smaller than jars.
units.literal: This is the so-called "Yangzhou smashes — Wuxing overturns pots"; pots are earthenware smaller than jars.

units.zh: 明帝太甯初，童謠曰：「惻惻力力，放馬山側。
units.en: Early Emperor Ming's Taining years a rhyme said: "Sighing, straining — loose horses on the hillside.
units.literal: Early Emperor Ming's Taining years a rhyme said: "Sighing, straining — loose horses on the hillside.

units.zh: 大馬死，小馬餓。
units.en: Great horse dies, small horse starves.
units.literal: Great horse dies, small horse starves.

units.zh: 高山崩，石自破。」
units.en: High mountain collapses; stones break themselves."
units.literal: High mountain collapses; stones break themselves."

units.zh: 及明帝崩，成帝幼，為蘇峻所逼，遷於石頭，禦膳不足，此「大馬死，小馬餓」也。
units.en: When Emperor Ming died Emperor Cheng was young, forced by Su Jun to move to Stone City with short rations — this is "great horse dies, small horse starves."
units.literal: When Emperor Ming died Emperor Cheng was young, forced by Su Jun to move to Stone City with short rations — this is "great horse dies, small horse starves."

units.zh: 高山，峻也，又言峻尋死。
units.en: Gao shan punned on Su Jun's name and doom.
units.literal: "High mountain" is Jun; it also says Jun soon died.

units.zh: 石，峻弟蘇石也。
units.en: The stone line targeted Su Jun's brother Su Shi.
units.literal: "Stone" is Su Shi, Su Jun's younger brother.

units.zh: 峻死後，石據石頭，尋為諸公所破，復是崩山石破之應也。
units.en: Su Shi's brief hold on Shitou completed the prophecy.
units.literal: After Jun died Shi held Stone City but was soon broken by the lords — again the omen of collapsing mountain and splitting stone.

units.zh: 成帝之末，又有童謠曰：「礚礚何隆隆，駕車入梓宮。」
units.en: Late Emperor Cheng another rhyme said: "Clang-clang, how it rumbles — driving a carriage into the cedar palace."
units.literal: Late Emperor Cheng another rhyme said: "Clang-clang, how it rumbles — driving a carriage into the cedar palace."

units.zh: 少日而宮車晏駕。
units.en: The emperor died almost at once.
units.literal: Within days the imperial carriage halted.

units.zh: 咸康二年十二月，河北謠云：「麥入土，殺石武。」
units.en: Xiankang 2, twelfth month — a Hebei rhyme said, “Wheat enters the earth; kill Shi Wu (Shi Hu).”
units.literal: Xiankang 2, twelfth month — a Hebei rhyme said, “Wheat enters the earth; kill Shi Wu (Shi Hu).”

units.zh: 後如謠言。
units.en: Shi Hu's fate matched the wheat curse.
units.literal: Later it happened as the rhyme said.

units.zh: 庾亮初鎮武昌，出至石頭，百姓于岸上歌曰：「庾公上武昌，翩翩如飛鳥。
units.en: When Yu Liang first garrisoned Wuchang and came out to Shitou, the people on the bank sang: "Lord Yu goes up to Wuchang, fluttering like a flying bird.
units.literal: When Yu Liang first garrisoned Wuchang and came out to Shitou, the people on the bank sang: "Lord Yu goes up to Wuchang, fluttering like a flying bird.

units.zh: 庾公還揚州，白馬牽旒旐。」
units.en: Lord Yu returns to Yangzhou — white horse draws mourning banners."
units.literal: Lord Yu returns to Yangzhou — white horse draws mourning banners."

units.zh: 又曰：「庾公初上時，翩翩如飛烏。
units.en: It also said: "When Lord Yu first went up, fluttering like a flying crow.
units.literal: It also said: "When Lord Yu first went up, fluttering like a flying crow.

units.zh: 庾公還揚州，白馬牽流蘇。」
units.en: Lord Yu returns to Yangzhou — white horse pulls tassels."
units.literal: Lord Yu returns to Yangzhou — white horse pulls tassels."

units.zh: 後連征不入，及薨於鎮，以喪還都葬，皆如謠言。
units.en: Yu Liang died at his post and came home for burial on cue.
units.literal: Later repeated summons failed; he died in post and his bier returned to the capital for burial — all as the rhymes said.

units.zh: 穆帝升平中，童兒輩忽歌於道曰《阿子聞》，曲終輒云「阿子汝聞不」？
units.en: Mid-Shengping Emperor Mu, children suddenly sang on the road "Az-zi hears"; after each tune they asked "Az-zi, did you hear?"
units.literal: Mid-Shengping Emperor Mu, children suddenly sang on the road "Az-zi hears"; after each tune they asked "Az-zi, did you hear?"

units.zh: 無幾而帝崩，太后哭之曰：「阿子汝聞不？」
units.en: Soon the emperor died; the empress dowager wept, "Azi, did you hear?"
units.literal: Soon the emperor died; the empress dowager wept, "Azi, did you hear?"

units.zh: 升平末，俗間忽作《廉歌》，有扈謙者聞之曰：「廉者，臨也。
units.en: Late Shengping folk suddenly sang the "Integrity Song"; Hu Qian heard it and said: "Integrity means 'overlooking.
units.literal: Late Shengping folk suddenly sang the "Integrity Song"; Hu Qian heard it and said: "Integrity means 'overlooking.

units.zh: 歌云『白門廉，宮庭廉』，內外悉臨，國家其大諱乎！」
units.en: The song runs "White Gate integrity, palace integrity" — inside and out all watched; is this not the state's great taboo!"
units.literal: The song runs "White Gate integrity, palace integrity" — inside and out all watched; is this not the state's great taboo!"

units.zh: 少時而穆帝晏駕。
units.en: Mu-di followed within months.
units.literal: Soon Emperor Mu passed.

units.zh: 哀帝隆和初，童謠曰：「昇平不滿斗，隆和那得久！
units.en: Early Longhe Emperor Ai, a rhyme said: "Shengping does not fill a dou — how can Longhe last!
units.literal: Early Longhe Emperor Ai, a rhyme said: "Shengping does not fill a dou — how can Longhe last!

units.zh: 桓公入石頭，陛下徒跣走。」
units.en: Lord Huan enters Stone City; Your Majesty runs barefoot."
units.literal: Lord Huan enters Stone City; Your Majesty runs barefoot."

units.zh: 朝廷聞而惡之，改年曰興寧。
units.en: Ministers renamed the year to dodge the curse.
units.literal: The court loathed it and changed the era to Xingning.

units.zh: 人復歌曰：「雖復改興寧，亦復無聊生。」
units.en: People sang again: "Even if you change to Xingning, life stays empty."
units.literal: People sang again: "Even if you change to Xingning, life stays empty."

units.zh: 哀旁壽崩。
units.en: Emperor Ai died young, fulfilling the bitter rhymes.
units.literal: Emperor Ai died young.

units.zh: 昇平五年而穆帝崩，「不滿斗」，昇平不至十年也。
units.en: Emperor Mu died in Shengping 5 — "does not fill a dou" — Shengping did not reach ten years.
units.literal: Emperor Mu died in Shengping 5 — "does not fill a dou" — Shengping did not reach ten years.

units.zh: 海西公太和中，百姓歌曰：「青青御路楊，白馬紫遊韁。
units.en: Under Duke Haixi's Taihe years the people sang: "Green-green willows on the imperial road — white horse with purple reins.
units.literal: Under Duke Haixi's Taihe years the people sang: "Green-green willows on the imperial road — white horse with purple reins.

units.zh: 汝非皇太子，那得甘露漿？」
units.en: You are not crown prince — how get sweet-dew nectar?"
units.literal: You are not crown prince — how get sweet-dew nectar?"

units.zh: 識者曰：「白者，金行，馬者，國族。
units.en: Those who understood said: "White is metal phase; horse is the dynastic clan.
units.literal: Those who understood said: "White is metal phase; horse is the dynastic clan.

units.zh: 紫為奪正之色，明以紫間硃也。」
units.en: Purple is the hue that usurps orthodoxy — it shows purple wedged between cinnabar."
units.literal: Purple is the hue that usurps orthodoxy — it shows purple wedged between cinnabar."

units.zh: 海西公尋廢，其三子並非海西公之子，縊以馬韁。
units.en: The Duke of Haixi was soon deposed; his three sons, said not to be his, were strangled with horse reins.
units.literal: Duke Haixi was soon deposed; his three sons were not truly his — they were strangled with horse reins.

units.zh: 死之明日，南方獻甘露馬。
units.en: A tribute horse arrived ironically named for the nectar line.
units.literal: The day after their deaths the south presented a "sweet dew" horse.

units.zh: 太和末，童謠曰：「犁牛耕御路，白門種小麥。」
units.en: Late Taihe a rhyme said: "Plow-oxen till the imperial road — white gate sows wheat."
units.literal: Late Taihe a rhyme said: "Plow-oxen till the imperial road — white gate sows wheat."

units.zh: 及海西公被廢，百姓耕其門以種小麥，遂如謠言。
units.en: When Duke Haixi was cast off, the people plowed his gate to plant wheat — thus the rhyme.
units.literal: When Duke Haixi was cast off the people plowed his gate to plant wheat — thus the rhyme.

units.zh: 海西公初生皇子，百姓歌云：「鳳皇生一雛，天下莫不喜。
units.en: When Duke Haixi first sired an heir-prince the people sang: "A phoenix hatches one chick — none under heaven fails to rejoice.
units.literal: When Duke Haixi first sired an heir-prince the people sang: "A phoenix hatches one chick — none under heaven fails to rejoice.

units.zh: 本言是馬駒，今定成龍子。」
units.en: Originally called a colt — now fixed as a dragon's son."
units.literal: Originally called a colt — now fixed as a dragon's son."

units.zh: 其歌甚美，其旨甚微。
units.en: The ode sounded sweet but hinted darkly.
units.literal: The song was lovely; its meaning was subtle.

units.zh: 海西公不男，使左右向龍與內侍接，生子，以為己子。
units.en: Duke Haixi was not virile; he had attendants Xianglong and eunuchs couple to bear sons he claimed as his own.
units.literal: Duke Haixi was not virile; he had attendants Xianglong and eunuchs couple to bear sons he claimed as his own.

units.zh: 桓石民為荊州，鎮上明，百姓忽歌曰「黃曇子」。
units.en: When Huan Shimin governed Jingzhou from Shangming the people suddenly sang "Lord Yellow Dusk."
units.literal: When Huan Shimin governed Jingzhou from Shangming the people suddenly sang "Lord Yellow Dusk."

units.zh: 曲中又曰：「黃曇英，揚州大佛來上明。」
units.en: The tune added: "Lord Yellow Blossom — Yangzhou's Great Buddha comes to Shangming."
units.literal: The tune added: "Lord Yellow Blossom — Yangzhou's Great Buddha comes to Shangming."

units.zh: 頃之而桓石民死，王忱為荊州。
units.en: Shimin died; Wang Chen replaced him.
units.literal: Soon Huan Shimin died and Wang Chen took Jingzhou.

units.zh: 黃曇子乃是王忱字也。
units.en: Huang Tanzi was Chen's style.
units.literal: "Yellow Dusk" was Wang Chen's courtesy name.

units.zh: 忱小字佛大，是「大佛來上明」也。
units.en: Chen's childhood name was Buddha-large — that is "Great Buddha comes to Shangming."
units.literal: Chen's childhood name was Buddha-large — that is "Great Buddha comes to Shangming."

units.zh: 孝武帝太元末，京口謠曰：「黃雌雞，莫作雄父啼。
units.en: Late Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan years Jingkou sang: "Yellow hen, don't crow like a cock-father.
units.literal: Late Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan years Jingkou sang: "Yellow hen, don't crow like a cock-father.

units.zh: 一旦去毛衣，衣被拉颯棲。」
units.en: Once feather-coat is shed, robes trail in tatters."
units.literal: Once feather-coat is shed, robes trail in tatters."

units.zh: 尋而王恭起兵誅王國寶，旋為劉牢之所敗，故言「拉颯棲」也。
units.en: Soon Wang Gong raised troops to kill Wang Guobao, then Liu Laozhi defeated him — hence "trail in tatters."
units.literal: Soon Wang Gong raised troops to kill Wang Guobao, then Liu Laozhi defeated him — hence "trail in tatters."

units.zh: 會稽王道子於東府造土山，名曰靈秀山。
units.en: Daozi piled Lingxiu Hill beside his yamen.
units.literal: Prince Kuaiji Sima Daozi built an earthen hill at the Eastern Bureau named Mount Lingxiu.

units.zh: 無幾而孫恩作亂，再踐會稽。
units.en: Sun En's revolt ravaged Kuaiji twice.
units.literal: Before long Sun En rebelled and twice trampled Kuaiji.

units.zh: 會稽，道子所封；
units.en: The commandery was Dao-zi's appanage.
units.literal: Kuaiji was Daozi's fief;

units.zh: 靈秀，孫恩之字也
units.en: The hill name duplicated Sun En's cognomen.
units.literal: Lingxiu was Sun En's style name.

units.zh: 庾楷鎮曆陽，百姓歌曰：「重羅黎，重羅黎，使君南上無還時。」
units.en: When Yu Kai held Liyang the people sang: "Layered gauze Li, layered gauze Li — when the lord goes south he never returns."
units.literal: When Yu Kai held Liyang the people sang: "Layered gauze Li, layered gauze Li — when the lord goes south he never returns."

units.zh: 後楷南奔桓玄，為玄所誅。
units.en: Yu Kai ran to Xuan and died for it.
units.literal: Later Kai fled south to Huan Xuan and Xuan executed him.

units.zh: 殷仲堪在荊州，童謠曰：「芒籠目，繩縛腹。
units.en: Yin Zhongkan in Jingzhou — a rhyme said: "Awn hoods the eyes, rope binds the belly.
units.literal: Yin Zhongkan in Jingzhou — a rhyme said: "Awn hoods the eyes, rope binds the belly.

units.zh: 殷當敗，桓當復。」
units.en: Yin must fall; Huan will rise."
units.literal: Yin must fall; Huan will rise."

units.zh: 未幾而仲堪敗，桓玄遂有荊州。
units.en: Soon Zhongkan fell and Huan Xuan took Jingzhou.
units.literal: Soon Zhongkan fell and Huan Xuan took Jingzhou.

units.zh: 王恭鎮京口，舉兵誅王國寶。
units.en: Wang Gong marched from Jingkou against Guobao.
units.literal: Wang Gong held Jingkou and raised troops to execute Wang Guobao.

units.zh: 百姓謠云：「昔年食白飯，今年食麥麩。
units.en: The people rhymed: "Last year we ate white rice; this year we eat wheat bran.
units.literal: The people rhymed: "Last year we ate white rice; this year we eat wheat bran.

units.zh: 天公誅謫汝，教汝撚嚨喉。
units.en: Heaven punishes you — it teaches you to clutch your throat.
units.literal: Heaven punishes you — it teaches you to clutch your throat.

units.zh: 嚨喉喝復喝，京口敗復敗。」
units.en: Throat choked again and again — Jingkou defeat upon defeat."
units.literal: Throat choked again and again — Jingkou defeat upon defeat."

units.zh: 識者曰：「昔年食白飯，言得志也。
units.en: Those who understood said: "Last year's white rice meant he had his way.
units.literal: Those who understood said: "Last year's white rice meant he had his way.

units.zh: 今年食麥麩，麩粗穢，其精已去，明將敗也，天公將加譴謫而誅之也。
units.en: This year's bran is coarse dregs; its essence is gone — it shows he will fall; Heaven will punish and kill.
units.literal: This year's bran is coarse dregs; its essence is gone — it shows he will fall; Heaven will punish and kill.

units.zh: 撚嚨喉，氣不通，死之祥也。
units.en: "Clutching throat" means breath blocked — an omen of death.
units.literal: "Clutching throat" means breath blocked — an omen of death.

units.zh: 敗復敗，丁寧之辭也。」
units.en: Defeat upon defeat" is emphatic wording."
units.literal: Defeat upon defeat" is emphatic wording."

units.zh: 恭尋死，京都又大行欬疾，而喉並喝焉。
units.en: Wang Gong fell while Jiankang coughed itself raw.
units.literal: Gong soon died; the capital also suffered a great cough-plague; throats were all hoarse.

units.zh: 王恭在京口，百姓間忽云：「黃頭小兒欲作賊，阿公在城，下指縛得。」
units.en: When Wang Gong was at Jingkou the people suddenly said: "Yellow-head lad wants to rebel — grandpa is in the city; point down and bind him."
units.literal: When Wang Gong was at Jingkou the people suddenly said: "Yellow-head lad wants to rebel — grandpa is in the city; point down and bind him."

units.zh: 又云：「黃頭小人欲作亂，賴得金刀作籓扞。」
units.en: They also said: "Yellow-head urchin plots trouble — thank the golden blade for defense."
units.literal: They also said: "Yellow-head urchin plots trouble — thank the golden blade for defense."

units.zh: 黃字上恭字頭也，小人恭字下也，尋如謠言者焉。
units.en: The charade split Wang Gong's name into yellow crown and petty man.
units.literal: Yellow" is the top of Gong's graph; "small man" is the bottom of Gong — soon it happened as spoken.

units.zh: 安帝隆安中，百姓忽作《懊憹》之歌，其曲曰：「草生可攬結，女兒可攬擷。」
units.en: Mid-Longan Emperor An the people suddenly sang the "Ao-nang" song; its tune ran: "Grass grows — you can braid it; girls grow — you can pick them."
units.literal: Mid-Longan Emperor An the people suddenly sang the "Ao-nang" song; its tune ran: "Grass grows — you can braid it; girls grow — you can pick them."

units.zh: 尋而桓玄篡位，義旗以三月二日掃定京都，誅之。
units.en: On the second day of the third month the righteous banners swept and secured the capital and executed Xuan.
units.literal: Soon Huan Xuan usurped; the righteous host swept the capital on the second day of the third month and executed him.

units.zh: 玄之宮女及逆党之家子女妓妾悉為軍賞，東及甌越，北流淮泗，皆人有所獲。
units.en: Victors parceled out Xuan's harem across the southeast.
units.literal: Xuan's palace women and rebel households' daughters and concubines all became army spoils — east to Ou-Yue, north along Huai-Si — everyone took a share.

units.zh: 故言時則草可結，事則女可擷也。
units.en: The song's double entendre matched wartime rape and plunder.
units.literal: Hence the saying: then grass could be tied; in the event girls could be plucked.

units.zh: 桓玄既篡，童謠曰：「草生及馬腹，烏啄桓玄目。」
units.en: After Huan Xuan seized the throne a rhyme said: "Grass grows to the horse's belly; crows peck Huan Xuan's eyes."
units.literal: After Huan Xuan seized the throne a rhyme said: "Grass grows to the horse's belly; crows peck Huan Xuan's eyes."

units.zh: 及玄敗，走至江陵，時正五月中，誅如其期焉。
units.en: His fifth-month death answered the crow omen.
units.literal: When Xuan fell he fled to Jiangling; it was exactly the fifth month — the execution matched the season.

units.zh: 安帝義熙初，童謠曰：「官家養蘆化成荻，蘆生不止自成積。」
units.en: Early Yixi Emperor An a children's rhyme said: "The court raises reeds that turn to stalk-grass; reeds grow without end and pile of themselves."
units.literal: Early Yixi Emperor An a children's rhyme said: "The court raises reeds that turn to stalk-grass; reeds grow without end and pile of themselves."

units.zh: 其時官養盧龍，寵以金紫，奉以名州，養之極也。
units.en: Lu Long won rank and region for doing nothing.
units.literal: At the time the court coddled Lu Long with gold-purple ribbons and a great province — the utmost indulgence.

units.zh: 而龍不能懷我好音，舉兵內伐，遂成仇敵也。
units.en: He repaid favor with rebellion.
units.literal: Yet Long could not cherish our good faith; he raised arms inward and became an enemy.

units.zh: 「蘆生不止自成積」，及盧龍之敗，斬伐其黨，猶如草木以成積也。
units.en: "Reeds pile endlessly" — when Lu Long fell his faction was cut down like stacked grass.
units.literal: "Reeds pile endlessly" — when Lu Long fell his faction was cut down like stacked grass.

units.zh: 盧龍據廣州，人為之謠曰：「蘆生漫漫竟天半。」
units.en: Lu Long held Guangzhou; people sang for him: "Reeds grow vast — they reach halfway to heaven."
units.literal: Lu Long held Guangzhou; people sang for him: "Reeds grow vast — they reach halfway to heaven."

units.zh: 後擠上流數州之地，內逼京輦，應「天半」之言。
units.en: Later he squeezed several upper provinces and pressed the capital — answering "half the sky."
units.literal: Later he squeezed several upper provinces and pressed the capital — answering "half the sky."

units.zh: 義熙二年，小兒相逢於道，輒舉其兩手曰「盧健健」，次曰「鬥歎鬥歎」，末曰「翁年老翁年老」。
units.en: Yixi 2: children meeting on the road would raise both hands crying "Lu is hale," then "battle and sigh," and lastly, "the elder is aged."
units.literal: Yixi 2: children meeting on the road would raise both hands crying "Lu is hale," then "battle and sigh," and lastly, "the elder is aged."

units.zh: 當時莫知所謂。
units.en: Contemporaries puzzled over the chant.
units.literal: No one then knew what it meant.

units.zh: 其後盧龍內逼，舟艦蓋川，「健健」之謂也。
units.en: Later Lu Long pressed inward; ships covered the streams — that is "strong-strong."
units.literal: Later Lu Long pressed inward; ships covered the streams — that is "strong-strong."

units.zh: 既至查浦，屢克期欲與官鬥，「鬥歎」之應也。
units.en: Reaching Chapu he repeatedly set battle dates with the court — the answer to "fight-sigh."
units.literal: Reaching Chapu he repeatedly set battle dates with the court — the answer to "fight-sigh."

units.zh: 「翁年老」，群公有期頤之慶，知妖逆之徒自然消殄也。
units.en: "Old man old" — ministers enjoyed their longevity; they knew the rebels would perish of themselves.
units.literal: "Old man old" — ministers enjoyed their longevity; they knew the rebels would perish of themselves.

units.zh: 其時復有謠言曰；
units.en: Another fragment circulated.
units.literal: Then another rumor said:

units.zh: 「盧橙橙，逐水流，東風忽如起，那得入石頭！」
units.en: "Lu orange-orange, drifting with the current — east wind suddenly rises — how can you enter Stone City!"
units.literal: "Lu orange-orange, drifting with the current — east wind suddenly rises — how can you enter Stone City!"

units.zh: 盧龍果敗，不得入石頭也。
units.en: Lu Long indeed lost and never entered Stone City.
units.literal: Lu Long indeed lost and never entered Stone City.

units.zh: 昔溫嶠令郭景純卜己與庾亮吉凶，景純云：「元吉。」
units.en: Once Wen Qiao had Guo Pu divine his and Yu Liang's fortune; Pu said: "Supremely auspicious."
units.literal: Once Wen Qiao had Guo Pu divine his and Yu Liang's fortune; Pu said: "Supremely auspicious."

units.zh: 嶠語亮曰：「景純每筮是，不敢盡言。
units.en: Qiao told Liang: "Whenever Pu divines thus he never speaks the whole truth.
units.literal: Qiao told Liang: "Whenever Pu divines thus he never speaks the whole truth.

units.zh: 吾等與國家同安危，而曰『元吉』，是事有成也。」
units.en: We share the state's peril; if he says 'supremely auspicious,' the affair will succeed."
units.literal: We share the state's peril; if he says 'supremely auspicious,' the affair will succeed."

units.zh: 於是協同討滅王敦。
units.en: They moved together against Wang Dun.
units.literal: Thereupon they jointly campaigned and destroyed Wang Dun.

units.zh: 苻堅初，童謠云：「阿堅連牽三十年，後若欲敗時，當在江湖邊。」
units.en: Early Fu Jian a rhyme said: "A-Jian drags on thirty years; when defeat comes it will be by rivers and lakes."
units.literal: Early Fu Jian a rhyme said: "A-Jian drags on thirty years; when defeat comes it will be by rivers and lakes."

units.zh: 及堅在位凡三十年，敗于淝水，是其應也。
units.en: His Fei River rout matched the prophecy.
units.literal: When Jian had reigned thirty years he lost at the Fei River — the fulfillment.

units.zh: 又謠語云：「河水清復清，苻堅死新城。」
units.en: Another ditty ran: "River water clears and clears again — Fu Jian dies in New City."
units.literal: Another ditty ran: "River water clears and clears again — Fu Jian dies in New City."

units.zh: 及堅為姚萇所殺，死於新城。
units.en: Yao Chang slew him in Xincheng.
units.literal: When Jian was killed by Yao Chang he died at New City.

units.zh: 復謠歌云：「魚羊田升當滅秦。」
units.en: Still another sang: "Fish-sheep field-rise shall destroy Qin."
units.literal: Still another sang: "Fish-sheep field-rise shall destroy Qin."

units.zh: 識者以為「魚羊，鮮也；
units.en: Readers thought "fish plus sheep" forms the graph for the Xianbei ethnonym;
units.literal: Readers thought "fish plus sheep" forms the graph for the Xianbei ethnonym;

units.zh: 田升，卑也，堅自號秦，言滅之者鮮卑也。」
units.en: "field-rise" means lowly; Jian styled himself Qin — it meant destroyers would be the Xianbei.
units.literal: "field-rise" means lowly; Jian styled himself Qin — it meant destroyers would be the Xianbei.

units.zh: 其群臣諫堅，令盡誅鮮卑，堅不從。
units.en: Courtiers begged genocide; Fu Jian demurred.
units.literal: His ministers urged Jian to exterminate the Xianbei; Jian refused.

units.zh: 及淮南敗還，初為慕容沖所攻，又為姚萇所殺，身死國滅。
units.en: Murong Chong and Yao Chang finished him after Feishui.
units.literal: After the Huainan defeat Murong Chong first struck him, then Yao Chang killed him — body dead, state gone.

units.zh: （分段）
units.en: Editorial divider before the next rubric.
units.literal: (Sectional marker in the received text.)

units.zh: 毛蟲之孽
units.en: Subsection: omens of furry vermin.
units.literal: Calamities from hairy creatures.

units.zh: （分段）
units.en: Divider.
units.literal: (Sectional marker in the received text.)

units.zh: 武帝太康六年，南陽獻兩足猛獸，此毛蟲之孽也。
units.en: In Taikang 6 under Emperor Wu, Nanyang offered a two-legged beast, classed here as a hairy-creature calamity.
units.literal: Emperor Wu, Taikang 6 — Nanyang presented a two-legged fierce beast; this was a calamity from hairy creatures.

units.zh: 識者為其文曰：「武形有虧，金獸失儀，聖主應天，期異何為！」
units.en: Readers glossed its pattern: "Martial form is flawed; metal beast loses propriety; sage lord answers Heaven — why this strangeness?"
units.literal: Readers glossed its pattern: "Martial form is flawed; metal beast loses propriety; sage lord answers Heaven — why this strangeness?"

units.zh: 言兆亂也。
units.en: They read it as rebellion brewing.
units.literal: It spoke of impending chaos.

units.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「足少者，下不勝任也。」
units.en: Jing Fang's Treatise on the Changes says: "Too few feet — those below cannot bear the burden."
units.literal: Jing Fang's Treatise on the Changes says: "Too few feet — those below cannot bear the burden."

units.zh: 干寶以為：「獸者陰精，居於陽，金獸也。
units.en: Gan Bao held: "Beasts are yin essences dwelling in yang — metal beasts.
units.literal: Gan Bao held: "Beasts are yin essences dwelling in yang — metal beasts.

units.zh: 南陽，火名也。
units.en: Nanyang is a fire name.
units.literal: Nanyang is a fire name.

units.zh: 金精入火而失其形，王室亂之妖也。」
units.en: Metal essence entering fire and losing shape is an omen of royal-house disorder."
units.literal: Metal essence entering fire and losing shape is an omen of royal-house disorder."

units.zh: 六，水數，言水數既極，火慝得作，而金受其敗也。
units.en: Numerology linked six to water's end and fire's revenge on metal.
units.literal: Six" is water's number — saying water's span is exhausted lets fire malice act while metal suffers defeat.

units.zh: 至元康九年，始殺太子，距此十四年。
units.en: Fourteen years later the heir died.
units.literal: By Yuankang 9 they first killed the crown prince — fourteen years from this omen.

units.zh: 二七十四，火始終相乘之數也。
units.en: The arithmetic omen paired twos and sevens with fire phases.
units.literal: Two times seven is fourteen — fire's beginning and end multiplied.

units.zh: 自帝受命，至湣懷之廢，凡三十五年焉。
units.en: Thirty-five years spanned Sima Yan to the ruined princes.
units.literal: From the emperor's mandate to Min and Huai's deposition was thirty-five years.

units.zh: 太康七年十一月丙辰，四角獸見於河間，河間王顒獲以獻。
units.en: In the seventh year of Taikang, Sima Yong sent up a quadruple-horned monster.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Taikang, eleventh month bingchen a horned beast with four corners appeared in Hejian; Prince Hejian Yong caught and presented it.

units.zh: 天戒若曰，角，兵象也，四者，四方之象，當有兵亂起于四方。
units.en: Four horns forecast multilateral rebellion.
units.literal: Heaven's warning: horns mean arms; four means the four directions — war will rise from every quarter.

units.zh: 後河間王遂連四方之兵，作為亂階，殆其應也。
units.en: Yong's coalition fulfilled the beast sign.
units.literal: Later Prince Hejian linked hosts from four directions and made rebellion — likely its answer.

units.zh: 懷帝永嘉五年，蝘鼠出延陵。
units.en: In Yongjia 5 under Emperor Huai, mole-crickets appeared at Yanling.
units.literal: Emperor Huai, Yongjia 5 — mole-crickets emerged at Yanling.

units.zh: 郭景純筮之曰：「此郡東之縣，當有妖人欲稱制者，亦尋自死矣。」
units.en: Guo Pu divined: "East of this commandery a man will claim imperial style; he will also soon die."
units.literal: Guo Pu divined: "East of this commandery a man will claim imperial style; he will also soon die."

units.zh: 其後吳興徐馥作亂，殺太守袁琇，馥亦時滅，是其應也。
units.en: Later Wuxing's Xu Fu rebelled, killed prefect Yuan Xiu; Fu perished quickly — the answer.
units.literal: Later Wuxing's Xu Fu rebelled, killed prefect Yuan Xiu; Fu perished quickly — the answer.

units.zh: 成帝咸和六年正月丁巳，會州郡秀孝于樂賢堂，有麏見於前，獲之。
units.en: On dingsi in the first month of Xianhe 6, a deer-like omen interrupted Emperor Cheng’s gathering of recommended scholars at Lexian Hall.
units.literal: Emperor Cheng, Xianhe 6, first month, dingsi — he assembled the provincial xiucai and xiaolian at Lexian Hall; a roe deer appeared before them and was captured.

units.zh: 孫盛以為吉祥。
units.en: Sun Sheng tried to read it as luck.
units.literal: Sun Sheng deemed it auspicious.

units.zh: 夫秀孝，天下之彥士；
units.en: The candidates were the empire's picked talent.
units.literal: Now excellence scholars are the realm's finest men;

units.zh: 樂賢堂，所以樂養賢也。
units.en: The hall's name celebrated sage cultivation.
units.literal: Lexian Hall is where the court delights in nurturing worthies.

units.zh: 自喪亂以後，風教陵夷，秀孝策試，乏四科之實。
units.en: Postwar exams had hollow essays.
units.literal: Since the turmoil manners decayed; examination essays lacked the four categories' substance.

units.zh: 麏興於前，或斯故乎？
units.en: The beast maybe mocked empty ritual.
units.literal: A zhang rising beforehand — perhaps for this reason?

units.zh: 哀帝隆和元年十月甲申，有麈入東海第。
units.en: On jiashen in the tenth month of Longhe 1, a zhu-deer entered the Donghai prince’s residence.
units.literal: Emperor Ai, Longhe 1, tenth month, jiashen — a zhu-deer entered the Donghai residence.

units.zh: 百姓歡言曰：「麈入東海第」，識者怪之。
units.en: The people cheered "A zhu enters Donghai mansion" — augurs found it strange.
units.literal: The people cheered "A zhu enters Donghai mansion" — augurs found it strange.

units.zh: 及海西廢為東海王，乃入其第。
units.en: When Haixi was demoted to Prince of Donghai he then entered that mansion.
units.literal: When Haixi was demoted to Prince of Donghai he then entered that mansion.

units.zh: 孝武太元十三年四月癸巳，祠廟畢，有兔行廟堂上。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowu, Taiyuan 13, fourth month, guisi — after the temple sacrifice was completed, a rabbit crossed the ancestral hall.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, Taiyuan 13, fourth month, guisi — after the temple sacrifice was completed, a rabbit crossed the ancestral hall.

units.zh: 天戒若曰，兔，野物也，而集宗廟之堂，不祥莫之甚焉。
units.en: Wild hares on the altar spelled extreme sacrilege.
units.literal: Heaven's warning: rabbits are wild things; for one to gather on the temple hall — no ill greater.

units.zh: （分段）
units.en: Divider before dog omens.
units.literal: (Sectional marker in the received text.)

units.zh: 犬禍
units.en: Subsection: canine portents.
units.literal: Dog disasters.

units.zh: （分段）
units.en: Divider.
units.literal: (Sectional marker in the received text.)

units.zh: 公孫文懿家有犬，冠幘絳衣上屋，此犬禍也。
units.en: A robed dog on the ridge mocked Wenyi's kingship bid.
units.literal: Gongsun Wenyi's household had a dog that capped itself in crimson robes and climbed the roof — a dog disaster.

units.zh: 屋上，亢陽高危之地。
units.en: Rooftops symbolized precarious pride.
units.literal: Roof is a high place of arrogant yang.

units.zh: 天戒若曰，亢陽無上，偷自尊高，狗而冠者也。
units.en: Heaven called the dog a crowned usurper.
units.literal: Heaven warns: arrogant yang without limit, stealing supreme honor — a dog wearing a cap.

units.zh: 及文懿自立為燕王，果為魏所滅。
units.en: When Wenyi declared himself Yan king, Wei destroyed him.
units.literal: When Wenyi declared himself Yan king Wei destroyed him.

units.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「君不正，臣欲篡，厥妖狗出朝門。」
units.en: Jing Fang's Treatise says: "When the lord is not upright ministers plot usurpation — the portent is dogs leaving the court gate."
units.literal: Jing Fang's Treatise says: "When the lord is not upright ministers plot usurpation — the portent is dogs leaving the court gate."

units.zh: 魏侍中應璩在直廬，欻見一白狗出門，問眾人，無見者。
units.en: Ying Qu alone glimpsed a phantom white hound.
units.literal: Wei attendant Ying Qu in the duty lodge suddenly saw a white dog leave the gate; he asked others — none saw it.

units.zh: 逾年卒，近犬禍也。
units.en: He perished a year later.
units.literal: He died within the year — near a dog disaster.

units.zh: 吳諸葛恪征淮南歸，將朝會，犬銜引其衣。
units.en: A dog tugged Zhuge Ke's gown before court.
units.literal: Wu's Zhuge Ke returning from Huainan campaign, about to court audience, a dog seized his robe.

units.zh: 恪曰：「犬不欲我行乎？」
units.en: Ke said: "Does the dog forbid me to go?"
units.literal: Ke said: "Does the dog forbid me to go?"

units.zh: 還坐。
units.en: He returned to his seat.
units.literal: He sat back down.

units.zh: 有頃復起，犬又銜衣，乃令逐犬，遂升車，入而被害。
units.en: Ignoring the second tug cost him his life at court.
units.literal: Soon he rose again; the dog seized his robe again; he ordered the dog driven off, mounted his carriage, entered and was killed.

units.zh: 武帝太康九年，幽州有犬，鼻行地三百餘步。
units.en: In Taikang 9 under Emperor Wu, a Youzhou dog was said to nose-walk more than three hundred paces.
units.literal: Emperor Wu, Taikang 9 — in Youzhou there was a dog that walked more than three hundred paces with its nose to the ground.

units.zh: 天戒若曰，是時帝不思和嶠之言，卒立惠帝，以致衰亂，是言不從之罰也。
units.en: Heaven's warning: then the emperor ignored He Jiao's advice, finally enthroned Emperor Hui, inviting decay — punishment for heedless words.
units.literal: Heaven's warning: then the emperor ignored He Jiao's advice, finally enthroned Emperor Hui, inviting decay — punishment for heedless words.

units.zh: 惠帝元康中，吳郡婁縣人家聞地中有犬子聲，掘之，得雌雄各一。
units.en: In Emperor Hui's Yuankang years a Lou county household heard puppy sounds underground; digging, they got a male and female.
units.literal: Emperor Hui Yuankang years a Lou county household heard puppy sounds underground; digging, they got a male and female.

units.zh: 還置窟中，覆以磨石，經宿失所在。
units.en: The pups vanished beneath the stone cover.
units.literal: They returned them to the pit, covered it with millstones; by morning they were gone.

units.zh: 天戒若曰，帝既衰弱，籓王相譖，故有犬禍。
units.en: The omen matched frail sovereignty and princely intrigue.
units.literal: Heaven warns: the emperor is weak; princes slander one another — hence dog disasters.

units.zh: 永興元年，丹陽內史硃逵家犬生三子，皆無頭。
units.en: In Yongxing 1, a dog in the household of Zhu Kui, Interior Minister of Danyang, gave birth to three pups, all without heads.
units.literal: Yongxing 1: Neishi Zhu Kui of Danyang had a dog whelp three pups, all headless.

units.zh: 後逵為揚州刺史曹武所殺。
units.en: Cao Wu executed him as predicted.
units.literal: Later Kui was killed by Yangzhou inspector Cao Wu.

units.zh: 孝懷帝永嘉五年，吳郡嘉興張林家狗人言云：「天下人餓死。」
units.en: Emperor Huai, Yongjia 5 — at Zhang Lin’s home in Jiaxing, Wu commandery, a dog spoke in human words, saying, “All the people under Heaven will starve to death.”
units.literal: Emperor Huai, Yongjia 5 — at Zhang Lin’s home in Jiaxing, Wu commandery, a dog spoke in human words, saying, “All the people under Heaven will starve to death.”

units.zh: 於是果有二胡之亂，天下饑荒焉。
units.en: The Five Barbarians' invasions fulfilled it.
units.literal: Thereupon indeed came the Two Hu calamities and empire-wide hunger.

units.zh: 湣帝建興元年，狗與豬交。
units.en: In Jianxing 1 under Emperor Min, dogs and pigs mated.
units.literal: Emperor Min, Jianxing 1 — dogs mated with pigs.

units.zh: 案《漢書》，景帝時有此，以為悖亂之氣，亦犬豕禍也。
units.en: Historians cited Han parallels for the abomination.
units.literal: The Book of Han records the same under Emperor Jing of Han, calling it perverse qi — also dog-and-pig disaster.

units.zh: 犬，兵革之占也。
units.en: Dogs foretold military upheaval.
units.literal: Dogs portend armor and war.

units.zh: 豕，北方匈奴之象。
units.en: Swine stood for steppe raiders.
units.literal: Pigs image the northern Xiongnu.

units.zh: 逆言失聽，異類相交，必生害也。
units.en: Unnatural unions mirrored a deaf court.
units.literal: When words rebel and hearing fails, different kinds coupling must breed harm.

units.zh: 餓而帝沒于胡，是其應也。
units.en: Sima Ye died in barbarian hands as predicted.
units.literal: Thereupon the emperor perished among the Hu — its fulfillment.

units.zh: 元帝太興中，吳郡太守張懋聞齋內床下犬聲，求而不得。
units.en: Zhang Mao's yamen hound that was not there.
units.literal: Mid-Taixing Emperor Yuan — Wu commandery prefect Zhang Mao heard dog sounds under his bedchamber bed but found nothing.

units.zh: 既而地自坼，見有二犬子，取而養之，皆死。
units.en: Earth-rend pups died under his care.
units.literal: Then the earth split; two puppies appeared; he took and raised them — both died.

units.zh: 尋而懋為沈充所害。
units.en: Shen Chong murdered him shortly after.
units.literal: Soon Mao was killed by Shen Chong.

units.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「讒臣在側，則犬生妖。」
units.en: Jing Fang's Treatise says: "When slanderers flank the throne, dogs breed portents."
units.literal: Jing Fang's Treatise says: "When slanderers flank the throne, dogs breed portents."

units.zh: 太興四年，廬江灊縣何旭家忽聞地中有犬子聲，掘之得一母犬，青釐色，狀甚羸瘦，走入草中，不知所在。
units.en: A subterranean bitch escaped He Xu's diggers.
units.literal: Taixing 4: He Xu's household in Qian county, Lujiang, heard puppy barks underground; digging, they found a bitch blue-gray, emaciated; she fled into grass and vanished.

units.zh: 視其處有二犬子，一雄一雌，哺而養之，雌死雄活。
units.en: One pup survived to adulthood.
units.literal: At the spot were two pups, male and female; they nursed them — the female died, the male lived.

units.zh: 及長為犬，善噬獸。
units.en: The survivor became a fierce hunter.
units.literal: Grown, it became a dog skilled at tearing beasts.

units.zh: 其後旭里中為蠻所沒。
units.en: Barbarians swallowed his village.
units.literal: Later Xu's hamlet was overrun by Man tribes.

units.zh: 安帝隆安初，吳郡治下狗恆夜吠，聚高橋上，人家狗有限而吠聲甚眾。
units.en: Early in Long'an under Emperor An, dogs under the Wu commandery seat constantly barked at night and gathered on Gao Bridge; households had only a limited number of dogs, yet the barking was very loud.
units.literal: Early Longan Emperor An, dogs under Wu commandery jurisdiction barked all night, massing on Gaobridge; household dogs were few yet the noise was huge.

units.zh: 或有夜覘視之云：「一狗假有兩三頭，皆前向亂吠。」
units.en: Night watchers said: "One dog seemed to have two or three heads, all barking forward."
units.literal: Night watchers said: "One dog seemed to have two or three heads, all barking forward."

units.zh: 無幾，孫恩亂于吳會焉。
units.en: Sun En's rebellion followed.
units.literal: Soon Sun En ravaged Wu and Kuaiji.

units.zh: 是時輔國將軍孫無終家于既陽，地中聞犬子聲，尋而地坼，有二犬子，皆白色，一雄一雌，取而養之，皆死。
units.en: Sun Wuzhong duplicated the underground pup omen.
units.literal: Then Fuguo general Sun Wuzhong at Jiyang heard puppy sounds underground; earth split; two white pups, male and female — raised, both died.

units.zh: 後無終為桓玄所誅滅。
units.en: Huan Xuan extirpated his line.
units.literal: Later Wuzhong was exterminated by Huan Xuan.

units.zh: 案《屍子》曰：「地中有犬，名曰地狼。」
units.en: The Shizi says: "There is a dog in earth called earth-wolf."
units.literal: The Shizi says: "There is a dog in earth called earth-wolf."

units.zh: 《夏鼎志》曰；
units.en: A second classic on buried dogs.
units.literal: The Xia Ding Record says:

units.zh: 「掘地得犬，名曰賈。」
units.en: "Dig earth and find a dog — call it Jia."
units.literal: "Dig earth and find a dog — call it Jia."

units.zh: 此蓋自然之物，不應出而出，為犬禍也。
units.en: Premature emergence meant canine ill omen.
units.literal: These are natural things; when they appear untimely it is dog disaster.

units.zh: 桓玄將拜楚王，已設拜席，群官陪位。
units.en: Xuan prepared his king-making ceremony.
units.literal: Huan Xuan was about to be invested Prince of Chu; the investiture mat was set; officials stood attendance.

units.zh: 玄未及出，有狗來便其席，莫不驚怪。
units.en: Before Xuan emerged a dog defecated on his mat — all were astounded.
units.literal: Before Xuan emerged a dog defecated on his mat — all were astounded.

units.zh: 玄性猜暴，竟無言者，逐狗改席而已。
units.en: Xuan was suspicious and violent; no one spoke; they drove off the dog and changed the mat.
units.literal: Xuan was suspicious and violent; no one spoke; they drove off the dog and changed the mat.

units.zh: 天戒若曰，桓玄無德而叨竊大位，故犬便其席，示其妄據之甚也。
units.en: Heaven warns: Huan Xuan lacks virtue yet steals high place — hence the dog fouled his mat, showing how false his seat was.
units.literal: Heaven warns: Xuan lacks virtue yet steals high place — hence the dog fouled his mat, showing how false his seat was.

units.zh: 八十日玄敗亡焉。
units.en: Within eighty days Xuan fell and died.
units.literal: Within eighty days Xuan fell and died.

units.zh: （分段）
units.en: Divider.
units.literal: (Sectional marker.)

units.zh: 白眚白祥
units.en: Subsection: pale anomalies.
units.literal: White ill-omens and white auspices.

units.zh: （分段）
units.en: Divider.
units.literal: (Sectional marker.)

units.zh: 魏明帝青龍三年正月乙亥，隕石于壽光。
units.en: On yihai in the first month of Qinglong 3 under Wei Emperor Ming, a meteorite fell at Shouguang.
units.literal: Wei Emperor Ming, Qinglong 3, first month, yihai — a meteorite fell at Shouguang.

units.zh: 案《左氏傳》「隕石，星也」，劉歆說曰：「庶眾惟星隕于宋者，象宋襄公將得諸侯而不終也。」
units.en: The Zuo Tradition says "falling stone is a star"; Liu Xin explained: "When many stars fell on Song it signified Duke Xiang gaining the hegemons yet not finishing."
units.literal: The Zuo Tradition says "falling stone is a star"; Liu Xin explained: "When many stars fell on Song it signified Duke Xiang gaining the hegemons yet not finishing."

units.zh: 秦始皇時有隕石，班固以為：「石，陰類也。
units.en: Qin Shihuang had meteorites; Ban Gu thought: "Stone is yin class.
units.literal: Qin Shihuang had meteorites; Ban Gu thought: "Stone is yin class.

units.zh: 又白祥，臣將危君。」
units.en: Also white omen — ministers will endanger the ruler."
units.literal: Also white omen — ministers will endanger the ruler."

units.zh: 是後宣帝得政云。
units.en: Sima Yi followed the omen.
units.literal: Thereafter Emperor Xuan seized power.

units.zh: 武帝太康五年五月丁巳，隕石于溫及河陽各二。
units.en: In Emperor Wu's Taikang 5, fifth month, day dingsi, two meteorites each fell at Wen and Heyang.
units.literal: Emperor Wu, Taikang 5, fifth month, dingsi — two meteorites each fell at Wen and Heyang.

units.zh: 六年正月，隕石于溫，三。
units.en: A second fall hit Wen commandery.
units.literal: Sixth year first month — meteorites at Wen, three.

units.zh: 成帝咸和八年五月，星隕於肥鄉，一。
units.en: In the fifth month of Xianhe 8 under Emperor Cheng, a single bolide fell at Feixiang.
units.literal: Emperor Cheng, Xianhe 8, fifth month — one star fell at Feixiang.

units.zh: 九年正月，隕石於涼州，二。
units.en: Liangzhou took two strikes.
units.literal: Ninth year first month — meteorites at Liangzhou, two.

units.zh: 吳孫亮五鳳二年五月，陽羨縣離裏山大石自立。
units.en: In the fifth month of Wufeng 2 under Wu’s Sun Liang, a great stone at Lili Mountain stood upright on its own.
units.literal: Wu Sun Liang, Wufeng 2, fifth month — a great stone at Lili Mountain in Yangxian county stood upright by itself.

units.zh: 案京房《易傳》曰「庶士為天子之祥也」，其說曰：「石立於山同姓，平地異姓。」
units.en: Jing Fang's Treatise says "commoners becoming Son of Heaven"; his gloss: "Stone on a mountain — same surname; on flat ground — different surname."
units.literal: Jing Fang's Treatise says "commoners becoming Son of Heaven"; his gloss: "Stone on a mountain — same surname; on flat ground — different surname."

units.zh: 干寶以為「孫皓承廢故之家得位，其應也。」
units.en: Gan Bao thought it meant, "Sun Hao inherited a deposed old house and gained the throne; this was its response."
units.literal: Gan Bao thought it meant, "Sun Hao inherited a deposed old house and gained the throne; this was its response."

units.zh: 或曰孫休見立之祥也。
units.en: Another reading favored Sun Xiu.
units.literal: Others say it signified Sun Xiu's enthronement.

units.zh: 武帝太康十年，洛陽宮西宜秋裏石生地中，始高三尺，如香鈩形，後如傴人，槃薄不可掘。
units.en: In Taikang 10 under Emperor Wu, a stone sprouted in Yiqiu ward west of the Luoyang palace, changing from an incense-burner shape into something like a hunched man.
units.literal: Emperor Wu, Taikang 10 — west of the Luoyang palace, in Yiqiu ward, a stone grew out of the ground; at first it was three chi high and shaped like an incense burner, later like a bent-over man, spreading thickly and impossible to dig out.

units.zh: 案劉向說，此白眚也。
units.en: Liu Xiang filed it under white shang.
units.literal: Liu Xiang's doctrine calls this white ill-omen.

units.zh: 明年宮車晏駕，王室始騷，卒以亂亡。
units.en: Sima Yan died; turmoil followed.
units.literal: Next year the imperial carriage halted; the royal house first stirred and ended in chaos.

units.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「石立如人，庶士為天下雄。」
units.en: Jing Fang says: "Stone stands like a man — commoners become heroes under heaven."
units.literal: Jing Fang says: "Stone stands like a man — commoners become heroes under heaven."

units.zh: 此近之矣。
units.en: The annalist judged it apt.
units.literal: This is close.

units.zh: 惠帝元康五年十二月，有石生於宜年裏。
units.en: In the twelfth month of Yuankang 5 under Emperor Hui, a stone grew in Yinian ward.
units.literal: Emperor Hui, Yuankang 5, twelfth month — a stone grew in Yinian ward.

units.zh: 永康元年，襄陽郡上言，得鳴石，撞之，聲聞七八里。
units.en: In Yongkang 1, Xiangyang Commandery reported finding ringing stones: when struck, their sound could be heard seven or eight li away.
units.literal: Yongkang 1 Xiangyang reported singing stones — struck, heard seven or eight li.

units.zh: 太安元年，丹陽湖熟縣夏架湖有大石，浮二百步而登岸，民驚噪相告曰：「石來。」
units.en: Tai'an 1 a great stone in Danyang Hushu county's Xiajia Lake floated two hundred paces then beached; folk cried "The stone comes."
units.literal: Tai'an 1 a great stone in Danyang Hushu county's Xiajia Lake floated two hundred paces then beached; folk cried "The stone comes."

units.zh: 干寶曰：「尋有石冰入建鄴。」
units.en: Gan Bao said: "Soon Shi Bing entered Jianye."
units.literal: Gan Bao said: "Soon Shi Bing entered Jianye."

units.zh: 車騎大將軍、東嬴王騰自并州遷鎮鄴，行次真定。
units.en: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Eastern Ying Teng Sima Teng moved his command from Bingzhou to garrison Ye, passing Zhengding en route.
units.literal: Cavalry general East Ying Prince Teng moved headquarters from Bingzhou to Ye, halting at Zhending.

units.zh: 時久積雪，而當門前方數丈獨消釋，騰怪而掘之，得玉馬，高尺許，口齒缺。
units.en: Melted snow revealed a toothless jade horse.
units.literal: Snow lay long yet several zhang before his gate alone melted; Teng wondered, dug, found a jade horse a chi tall with broken teeth.

units.zh: 騰以馬者國姓，上送之，以為瑞。
units.en: He offered the jade horse as a Sima totem.
units.literal: Teng thought horses were the dynastic surname and sent it up as auspicious.

units.zh: 然馬無齒則不得食，妖祥之兆，衰亡之征。
units.en: Toothless mount spelled hungry power.
units.literal: Yet a horse without teeth cannot eat — an omen both freakish and blessed, sign of decline.

units.zh: 案占，此白祥也。
units.en: Texts labeled it white xiang.
units.literal: Divination classifies this as white auspice.

units.zh: 是後騰為汲桑所殺，而天下遂亂。
units.en: Ji Sang slew him; anarchy spread.
units.literal: Afterward Teng was killed by Ji Sang and the realm slid into chaos.

units.zh: 武帝泰始八年五月，蜀地雨白毛，此白祥也。
units.en: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, white hair fell like rain in Shu, a white omen.
units.literal: Emperor Wu, Taishi 8, fifth month — white hair rained down in Shu; this was a white omen.

units.zh: 時益州刺史皇甫晏伐汶山胡，從事何旅固諫，不從，牙門張弘等困眾之怨，誣晏謀逆，害之。
units.en: Then Inspector Huangfu Yan campaigned against Wenshan Hu; aide He Lu counseled against it and was ignored; gate officer Zhang Hong exploited troop resentment, falsely accused Yan of treason, and killed him.
units.literal: Then Inspector Huangfu Yan campaigned against Wenshan Hu; aide He Lu counseled against it; ignored; gate officer Zhang Hong exploited troop hatred, slandered Yan as rebel, murdered him.

units.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「前樂後憂，厥妖天雨羽。」
units.en: Jing Fang says: "Joy before grief — its portent heaven rains feathers."
units.literal: Jing Fang says: "Joy before grief — its portent heaven rains feathers."

units.zh: 又曰：「邪人進，賢人逃，天雨毛。」
units.en: Also: "Villains advance, worthies flee — heaven rains fur."
units.literal: Also: "Villains advance, worthies flee — heaven rains fur."

units.zh: 其《易妖》曰：「天雨毛羽，貴人出走。」
units.en: His Omen Treatise says: "Heaven rains feather-fur — nobles flee."
units.literal: His Omen Treatise says: "Heaven rains feather-fur — nobles flee."

units.zh: 三占皆應。
units.en: Every reading converged.
units.literal: All three divinations fit.

units.zh: 惠帝永寧元年，齊王冏舉義軍。
units.en: In Yongning 1 under Emperor Hui, Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, raised his righteous army.
units.literal: Emperor Hui, Yongning 1 — Prince Jiong of Qi raised a righteous army.

units.zh: 軍中有小兒，出於襄城繁昌縣，年八歲，發體悉白，頗能卜，于《洪范》，白祥也。
units.en: An albino child divined in Jiong's host.
units.literal: Among the troops a boy from Xiangcheng Fanchang, age eight, all white-haired, could divine — per Hong Fan, white omen.

units.zh: 成帝咸康初，地生毛，近白祥也。
units.en: Early Emperor Cheng Xiankang — hair sprouted from earth — near white omen.
units.literal: Early Emperor Cheng Xiankang — hair sprouted from earth — near white omen.

units.zh: 孫盛以為人勞之異也。
units.en: Sun Sheng blamed human fatigue.
units.literal: Sun Sheng thought it exhaustion of the people.

units.zh: 是後石季龍滅而中原向化，將相皆甘心焉。
units.en: After Shi Jilong's fall the Central Plain turned toward civilization and generals and ministers were content.
units.literal: Thereafter Shi Jilong fell and the Central Plain turned toward civilization; generals and ministers were content.

units.zh: 於是方鎮屢革，邊戍仍遷，皆擁帶部曲，動有萬數。
units.en: Warlord militias multiplied on the borders.
units.literal: Then frontier commands rotated endlessly; garrisons shifted; each led private hosts numbering myriads.

units.zh: 其間征伐征賦，役無寧歲，天下勞擾，百姓疲怨。
units.en: Endless corvée enraged the north.
units.literal: Amid campaigns and levies no year knew rest; the world toiled; people wearied and resented.

units.zh: 咸康三年六月，地生毛。
units.en: In the sixth month of Xiankang 3, hair-like growth appeared on the ground.
units.literal: Xiankang 3, sixth month — the ground grew hair.

units.zh: 孝武太元二年五月，京都地生毛，至四年而氐賊次襄國，圍彭城，向廣陵，征戍仍出，兵連年不解。
units.en: In the fifth month of Taiyuan 2 under Emperor Xiaowu, the capital’s ground grew hair; by Taiyuan 4 the Di forces were threatening Xiangguo, Pengcheng, and Guangling, and campaigns dragged on year after year.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, Taiyuan 2, fifth month — the ground in the capital grew hair; by the fourth year, the Di rebels reached Xiangguo, besieged Pengcheng, and advanced toward Guangling, so expeditionary and garrison troops kept going out and the armies did not disengage for years.

units.zh: 太元十四年四月，京都地生毛。
units.en: In the fourth month of Taiyuan 14, the capital’s ground again grew hair.
units.literal: Taiyuan 14, fourth month — the ground in the capital grew hair.

units.zh: 是時苻堅滅後，經略多事，人勞之應也。
units.en: Post-Feishui scheming matched the sign.
units.literal: At the time after Fu Jian's fall planning multiplied — an omen of human exhaustion.

units.zh: 十七年四月，地生毛。
units.en: Taiyuan 17 repeated the anomaly.
units.literal: Seventeenth year fourth month — earth grew hair.

units.zh: 安帝隆安四年四月乙未，地生毛，或白或黑。
units.en: On yiwei in the fourth month of Long’an 4 under Emperor An, the ground sprouted both white and black hair-like growth.
units.literal: Emperor An, Long’an 4, fourth month, yiwei — the ground grew hair, some white and some black.

units.zh: 元興三年五月，江陵地生毛。
units.en: In the fifth month of Yuanxing 3, the ground at Jiangling grew hair.
units.literal: Yuanxing 3, fifth month — the ground at Jiangling grew hair.

units.zh: 是後江陵見襲，交戰者數矣。
units.en: The city saw serial sieges.
units.literal: Afterward Jiangling was attacked repeatedly — many battles.

units.zh: 義熙三年三月，地生白毛。
units.en: In the third year of Yixi, White filaments rose in spring.
units.literal: In the third year of Yixi, third month — earth grew white hair.

units.zh: 十年三月地生毛。
units.en: Yixi decade opened with turf beards.
units.literal: Tenth year third month earth grew hair.

units.zh: 明年，王旅西討司馬休之。
units.en: The royal army attacked Sima Xiuzhi in the west the year after.
units.literal: Next year royal troops marched west against Sima Xiuzhi.

units.zh: 又明年，北掃關洛。
units.en: A second campaign reclaimed the north.
units.literal: The year after that they swept Guan-Luo north.

units.zh: （分段）
units.en: Divider.
units.literal: (Sectional marker.)

units.zh: 木沴金
units.en: Subsection: wood overcoming metal.
units.literal: Wood harms metal.

units.zh: （分段）
units.en: Divider.
units.literal: (Sectional marker.)

units.zh: 魏齊王正始末，河南尹李勝治聽事，有小材激墮，楇受符吏石彪頭，斷之，此木沴金也。
units.en: Late in Zhengshi under the King of Qi of Wei, Henan Yin Li Sheng's audience hall: a splinter sprang loose, struck clerk Shi Biao's head and severed it — wood harming metal.
units.literal: Late Wei Qi King Zhengshi — Henan Yin Li Sheng's audience hall: a splinter sprang loose, struck clerk Shi Biao's head and severed it — wood harming metal.

units.zh: 勝後旬日而敗。
units.en: Li Sheng lost power immediately.
units.literal: Within ten days Sheng fell.

units.zh: 惠帝元康八年五月，郊禖壇石中破為二，此木沴金也。
units.en: In the fifth month of Yuankang 8 under Emperor Hui, the fertility altar stone split in two, read as wood harming metal.
units.literal: Emperor Hui, Yuankang 8, fifth month — the stone at the suburban fertility altar split in two; this was wood injuring metal.

units.zh: 郊禖壇者，求子之神位，無故自毀，太子將危之象也。
units.en: Broken altar spelled doom for the crown prince.
units.literal: The suburban Subs altar is the god-seat for seeking sons; it broke without cause — image of the heir in peril.

units.zh: 明年湣懷廢死。
units.en: The next year Minhuai (the crown prince) was deposed and died.
units.literal: Next year Min and Huai were deposed and died.

units.zh: 孝武帝太元十年四月，謝安出鎮廣陵，始發石頭，金鼓無故自破。
units.en: In the fourth month of Taiyuan 10, when Xie An left Shitou to take post at Guangling, the bronze drums burst on their own.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, Taiyuan 10, fourth month — Xie An went out to garrison Guangling; just as he set off from Shitou, the bronze drums split of themselves for no reason.

units.zh: 此木沴金之異也，天意也。
units.en: Metal drums failing showed cosmic reproof.
units.literal: This is the anomaly of wood harming metal — Heaven's intent.

units.zh: 天戒若曰，安徒揚經略之聲，終無其實，鉦鼓不用之象也。
units.en: Silent drums mocked empty strategy.
units.literal: Heaven warns: An boasted of campaigns yet achieved none — bells and drums unused.

units.zh: 月餘，以疾還而薨。
units.en: He died weeks later.
units.literal: Within a month he returned ill and died.

units.zh: 視之不明，是謂不哲
units.en: Section: blurred vision — lack of discernment.
units.literal: When sight is unclear it is called "not wise."

units.zh: 《傳》曰：「視之不明，是謂不哲，厥咎舒，厥罰恆燠，厥極疾。
units.en: The Commentary says: "When sight is not clear it is called lack of wisdom; its fault is slackness; its punishment constant heat; its extreme sickness.
units.literal: The Commentary says: "When sight is not clear it is called lack of wisdom; its fault is slackness; its punishment constant heat; its extreme sickness.

units.zh: 時則有草妖，時則有蠃蟲之孽，時則有羊禍，時則有目痾，時則有赤眚赤祥。
units.en: Then arise grass portents; then soft-shelled insect calamities; then sheep disasters; then eye diseases; then red ill-omens and red signs.
units.literal: Then arise grass portents; then soft-shelled insect calamities; then sheep disasters; then eye diseases; then red ill-omens and red signs.

units.zh: 惟水沴火。」
units.en: Only water harms fire."
units.literal: Only water harms fire."

units.zh: 視之不明，是謂不哲。
units.en: The refrain on benighted rule.
units.literal: When sight is not clear" is called lack of wisdom.

units.zh: 哲，知也。
units.en: Zhe glosses as understanding.
units.literal: "Wise" means to know.

units.zh: 《詩》云：「爾德不明，以亡陪亡卿。
units.en: The Book of Songs says: "Your virtue not bright — you lose aides, you lose ministers.
units.literal: The Book of Songs says: "Your virtue not bright — you lose aides, you lose ministers.

units.zh: 不明爾德，以亡背亡側。」
units.en: Not bright your virtue — you lose backs, you lose flanks."
units.literal: Not bright your virtue — you lose backs, you lose flanks."

units.zh: 言上不明，暗昧蔽惑，則不能知善惡，親近習，長同類，亡功者受賞，有罪者不殺，百官廢亂，失在舒緩，故其咎舒也。
units.en: Obscure sovereigns muddle personnel until bureaucracy collapses — the "slack" blame.
units.literal: It means when superiors are not clear, dark and deluded, they cannot know good and evil, favor cronies, promote their kind, reward the meritless, spare the guilty — the hundred offices rot; failure lies in slackness — hence the fault is "slack."

units.zh: 盛夏日長，暑以養物，政弛緩，故其罰常燠也。
units.en: Lax rule draws the scourge of endless summer.
units.literal: Midsummer days lengthen; heat nurtures things; government relaxes — hence the punishment is constant heat.

units.zh: 燠則冬溫，春夏不和，傷病疾人，其極疾也。
units.en: Mild winters and sickly seasons mark the nadir.
units.literal: When it is torrid, winter is warm, spring and summer discordant, injuring the sick — its extreme is sickness.

units.zh: 誅不行則霜不殺草，繇臣下則殺不以時，故有草妖。
units.en: Untimely justice lets weeds thrive — "grass omens."
units.literal: When executions fail frost does not kill grass; when fault lies with ministers killing is untimely — hence grass portents.

units.zh: 凡妖，貌則以服，言則以詩，聽則以聲。
units.en: Omens dress as costume, verse, or noise.
units.literal: Generally among portents appearance shows in dress, speech in songs, hearing in sound.

units.zh: 視不以色者，五色，物之大分也，在於眚祥，故聖人以為草妖，失物柄之明者也。
units.en: Because color vision fails, sages read plant freaks as blurred rule.
units.literal: Sight not by color — the five colors are the great allotment of things; ill-omens dwell there; hence sages treat freak grass as loss of clear sight.

units.zh: 溫燠生蟲，故有蠃蟲之孽，謂螟螣之類當死不死，當生而不生，或多於故而為災也。
units.en: Heat-born vermin mean soft-shell plagues.
units.literal: Warmth breeds insects — hence soft-shelled insect calamity: caterpillars that should die yet live, should live yet fail, or swarm beyond norm.

units.zh: 劉歆以為屬思心不容。
units.en: Liu Xin linked it to undisciplined thought.
units.literal: Liu Xin attributed it to a mind that will not contain itself.

units.zh: 于《易》，剛而苞柔為《離》，《離》為火，為目。
units.en: The Li hexagram pairs fire with the eye.
units.literal: In the Changes, hard wrapping soft is Li; Li is fire and eye.

units.zh: 羊上角下蹄，剛而苞柔，羊大目而不精明，視氣毀，故有羊禍。
units.en: Sheep embody dim vision — "sheep calamity."
units.literal: Sheep horn above hoof below — hard wrapping soft; sheep have big yet dull eyes — sight qi ruined — hence sheep disaster.

units.zh: 一日，暑歲羊多疫死，及為怪，亦是也。
units.en: Summer sheep epidemics count the same.
units.literal: One view: hot years sheep die in plague or act monstrous — that too.

units.zh: 及人，則多病目者，故有目痾。
units.en: Humanity suffers ocular plague.
units.literal: Among people many eye diseases — hence eye afflictions.

units.zh: 火色赤，故有赤眚赤祥。
units.en: Scarlet sky-wounds follow fire's phase.
units.literal: Fire's color is red — hence red ill-omens and red signs.

units.zh: 凡視傷者，病火氣；
units.en: Hurt vision means hurt flame-element.
units.literal: Whenever sight is injured, fire qi is sick.

units.zh: 火氣傷，則水沴之。
units.en: Water then overwhelms fire.
units.literal: When fire qi is hurt, water harms it.

units.zh: 其極疾者順之，其福曰壽。
units.en: Heal that worst and the boon is long life.
units.literal: For the extreme of sickness, if redressed, the blessing is called longevity.

units.zh: 劉歆《視傳》曰有羽蟲之孽，雞禍。
units.en: Liu Xin adds fowl portents.
units.literal: Liu Xin's Treatise on Sight adds feathered insect calamity and chicken disaster.

units.zh: 說以為于天文南方硃張為鳥星，故為羽蟲。
units.en: The Vermilion Bird mansion governs winged pests.
units.literal: Exegesis holds that in astronomy the southern Zhu-Zhang is the bird star — hence feathered insects.

units.zh: 禍亦從羽，故為雞。
units.en: Plumed ill luck targets poultry.
units.literal: Disaster follows feathers — hence chickens.

units.zh: 雞于《易》自在《巽》，說非是。
units.en: The chicken-Sun linkage is rejected.
units.literal: Chickens belong to Xun in the Changes — that gloss is wrong.

units.zh: 庶征之恆燠，劉向以為《春秋》無冰也。
units.en: Liu Xiang read perpetual warmth as iceless winters.
units.literal: Among lesser omens constant heat — Liu Xiang thought the Spring and Autumn records "no ice."

units.zh: 小燠不書，無冰然後書，舉其大者也。
units.en: Annalists note only total failure of winter freeze.
units.literal: Small heat is not written; only when there is no ice is it recorded — lifting the great case.

units.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「祿不遂行茲謂欺，廝咎燠。
units.en: Jing Fang's Treatise says: "When emoluments are not justly dispensed it is called deceit — its fault is heat.
units.literal: Jing Fang's Treatise says: "When emoluments are not justly dispensed it is called deceit — its fault is heat.

units.zh: 其燠，雨雲四至而溫。
units.en: Its heat: rain clouds come from four sides yet it stays warm.
units.literal: Its heat: rain clouds come from four sides yet it stays warm.

units.zh: 臣安祿樂逸茲謂亂，燠而生蟲。
units.en: When ministers are content and idle it is called disorder — heat breeds insects.
units.literal: When ministers are content and idle it is called disorder — heat breeds insects.

units.zh: 知罪不誅茲謂舒，其燠，夏則暑殺人，冬則物華實。
units.en: When known crimes go unpunished it is called slackness; its heat kills people in summer yet ripens fruit in winter.
units.literal: When known crimes go unpunished it is called slackness; its heat kills people in summer yet ripens fruit in winter.

units.zh: 重過不誅茲謂亡征，其咎當寒而燠盡六日也。」
units.en: When grave faults go unexecuted it is called omens of extinction; the fault should be cold yet heat lasts six full days."
units.literal: When grave faults go unexecuted it is called omens of extinction; the fault should be cold yet heat lasts six full days."

units.zh: 吳孫亮建興元年九月，桃李華，孫權世政煩賦重，人凋於役。
units.en: In Wu, in Sun Liang's Jianxing 1.9, peach and plum trees bloomed out of season; under Sun Quan, heavy taxes and service had already worn the people down.
units.literal: In Wu, in Sun Liang's Jianxing 1, ninth month, peach and plum trees blossomed; in Sun Quan's time, government was burdensome, taxes were heavy, and the people wasted away in service.

units.zh: 是時諸葛恪始輔政，息校官，原逋責，除關梁，崇寬厚，此舒緩之應也。
units.en: Ke's reforms briefly softened the regime — matching the omen.
units.literal: Then Zhuge Ke began assisting, halted secret police, forgave arrears, opened barriers, favored leniency — an answer of slackness.

units.zh: 一說桃李寒華為草妖，或屬華孽。
units.en: Some filed the blooms under "grass anomaly."
units.literal: Another view: peach-plum bloom in cold is grass portent or flower calamity.

units.zh: 魏少帝景元三年十月，桃李華。
units.en: In the tenth month of Jingyuan 3 under the young Wei emperor, peach and plum trees bloomed out of season.
units.literal: Wei Young Emperor, Jingyuan 3, tenth month — peach and plum trees blossomed.

units.zh: 時少帝深樹恩德，事崇優緩，此其應也。
units.en: His indulgent style explained the sign.
units.literal: Then the young emperor piled kindness and preferred lax rule — its answer.

units.zh: 惠帝元康二年二月，巴西郡界草皆生華，結子如麥，可食。
units.en: In the second month of Yuankang 2 under Emperor Hui, Baxi grasses flowered and set edible wheat-like seed.
units.literal: Emperor Hui, Yuankang 2, second month — grasses throughout Baxi commandery all flowered and bore seeds like wheat, which could be eaten.

units.zh: 時帝初即位，楚王瑋矯詔誅汝南王亮及太保衛瓘，帝不能察。
units.en: When the emperor had just taken the throne, Prince Chu Wei forged edicts to execute Prince Runan Liang and Grand Tutor Wei Guan, and the emperor could not see through it.
units.literal: The emperor had just mounted the throne; Prince Chu Wei forged edicts killing Prince Runan Liang and grand tutor Wei Guan — the emperor could not investigate.

units.zh: 今非時草結實，此恆燠寬舒之罰。
units.en: Untimely grain on weeds bespoke thermal slackness.
units.literal: Now grass fruits out of season — punishment of constant heat and lax ease.

units.zh: 穆帝永和九年十二月，桃李華，是時簡文輔政，事多馳略，舒緩之應也。
units.en: In the twelfth month of Yonghe 9 under Emperor Mu, peach and plum trees bloomed in winter, matching the lax administration while Jianwen assisted the government.
units.literal: Emperor Mu, Yonghe 9, twelfth month — peach and plum trees blossomed; at that time Jianwen assisted in government, and many affairs were lax and neglected; this was a response to slackness.

units.zh: （分段）
units.en: Divider.
units.literal: (Sectional marker.)

units.zh: 草妖
units.en: Subsection: vegetal omens.
units.literal: Grass portents.

units.zh: （分段）
units.en: Divider.
units.literal: (Sectional marker.)

units.zh: 漢獻帝建安二十五年春正月，魏武帝在洛陽起建始殿，伐濯龍樹而血出，又掘徙梨，根傷亦血出。
units.en: In the first month of spring, Jian’an 25, Cao Cao’s Luoyang construction drew blood from trees: the Zhuolong tree bled when cut, and a transplanted pear bled from its roots.
units.literal: Han Emperor Xian, Jian’an 25, spring, first month — Wei Emperor Wu was building Jianshi Hall in Luoyang; when the Zhuolong tree was cut, blood came out, and when a pear tree was dug up and moved, blood also came from its injured roots.

units.zh: 帝惡之，遂寢疾，是月崩。
units.en: He sickened and died the same month.
units.literal: The king loathed it, fell ill, died that month.

units.zh: 蓋草妖，又赤祥，是歲魏文帝黃初元年也。
units.en: The sign was classed as both a grass portent and a red omen, in the first year of Cao Pi’s Huangchu reign.
units.literal: This was probably a grass portent and also a red omen; that year was Wei Emperor Wen’s Huangchu 1.

units.zh: 吳孫亮五鳳元年六月，交阯稗草化為稻。
units.en: In the sixth month of Wufeng 1 under Sun Liang of Wu, Jiaozhi barnyard grass turned into rice.
units.literal: Wu Sun Liang, Wufeng 1, sixth month — barnyard grass in Jiaozhi changed into rice.

units.zh: 昔三苗將亡，五穀變種，此草妖也。
units.en: Ancient precedent: mutating crops meant doom.
units.literal: When the Three Miao were about to perish the five grains changed species — this is grass portent.

units.zh: 其後亮廢。
units.en: Sun Liang fell soon after.
units.literal: Afterward Liang was deposed.

units.zh: 蜀劉禪景耀五年，宮中大樹無故自折。
units.en: In Jingyao 5 under Liu Shan of Shu, a great palace tree broke without cause.
units.literal: Shu Liu Shan, Jingyao 5 — a great tree in the palace snapped by itself for no reason.

units.zh: 譙周憂之，無所與言，乃書柱曰：「眾而大，其之會。
units.en: Qiao Zhou fretted, spoke to no one, wrote on a pillar: "Many and great — there will be a gathering.
units.literal: Qiao Zhou fretted, spoke to no one, wrote on a pillar: "Many and great — there will be a gathering.

units.zh: 具而授，若何復。」
units.en: Complete then handed over — how can there be restoration?"
units.literal: Complete then handed over — how can there be restoration?"

units.zh: 言曹者眾也，魏者大也，眾而大，天下其當會也。
units.en: The riddle spelled Cao-Wei swallowing Shu.
units.literal: It means Cao is "many," Wei is "great"; many and great — the realm will unite.

units.zh: 具而授，如何復有立者乎？
units.en: No dynasty could follow once mandate was yielded.
units.literal: "Complete then handed over" — how could another house stand?

units.zh: 蜀果亡，如周言，此草妖也。
units.en: The tree break was vegetal omen.
units.literal: Shu indeed perished as Zhou said — grass portent.

units.zh: 吳孫皓天璽元年，吳郡臨平湖自漢末穢塞，是時一夕忽開除無草。
units.en: In Tianxi 1 under Sun Hao, Linping Lake, clogged since late Han, suddenly cleared overnight.
units.literal: Wu Sun Hao, Tianxi 1 — Linping Lake in Wu commandery had been fouled and blocked since the end of Han; at this time it suddenly cleared overnight and had no weeds.

units.zh: 長老相傳：此湖塞，天下亂；
units.en: Folk wisdom tied the lake to order.
units.literal: Elders handed down: when this lake blocks, the realm is chaotic;

units.zh: 此湖開，天下平。
units.en: An open lake meant unity.
units.literal: when it opens, the realm is at peace.

units.zh: 吳尋亡而九服為一。
units.en: Wu's conquest followed.
units.literal: Wu soon fell and the Nine Domains became one.

units.zh: 天紀三年八月，建鄴有鬼目菜于工黃狗家生，依緣棗樹，長丈餘，莖廣四寸，厚二分。
units.en: In the third year of Tianji, Weird vines sprouted on a craftsman's jujube.
units.literal: In the third year of Tianji, eighth month at Jianye "ghost-eye" greens grew at artisan Huang Gou's home, twining a jujube, over a zhang long, stem four cun wide, two fen thick.

units.zh: 又有蕒菜生工吳平家，高四尺，如枇杷形，上圓，徑一尺八寸，莖廣五寸，兩邊生葉，綠色。
units.en: A second freak crop rose at Wu Ping's door.
units.literal: Also "mai" greens grew at artisan Wu Ping's home, four chi high, loquat-shaped, round top, diameter one chi eight cun, stem five cun wide, leaves green on both sides.

units.zh: 東觀案圖，名鬼目作芝萆，蕒菜作平慮，遂以狗為侍芝郎，平為平慮郎，皆銀印青綬。
units.en: The court jokingly ennobled the plants and artisans.
units.literal: Eastern Archives checked charts: ghost-eye was titled zhi-cao, mai was titled "peace-calmer"; they made Gou herb attendant and Ping peace attendant — silver seal, blue ribbon.

units.zh: 干寶曰：明年平吳，王浚止船正得平渚，姓名顯然，指事之征也。
units.en: Gan Bao read the names as prophecy of conquest.
units.literal: Gan Bao said: next year Wu was pacified; Wang Jun moored exactly at Ping islet — names plainly pointed to the event.

units.zh: 黃狗者，吳以土運承漢，故初有黃龍之瑞。
units.en: Yellow stood for Wu's earth succession.
units.literal: Yellow dog — Wu, earth phase succeeding Han, first had yellow dragon omens.

units.zh: 及其季年，而有鬼目之妖托黃狗之家。
units.en: Late Wu paired yellow dogs with demon vines.
units.literal: In its final years ghost-eye portents lodged with a yellow dog household.

units.zh: 黃稱不改，而貴賤大殊，天道精微之應敢也。
units.en: Same hue, opposite fortune — Heaven's irony.
units.literal: The color name stayed yet noble and base inverted vastly — Heaven's subtle answer.

units.zh: 惠帝元康二年春，巴西郡界竹生花，紫色，結實如麥，外皮青，中赤白，味甘。
units.en: In spring of Yuankang 2 under Emperor Hui, Baxi bamboo flowered purple and fruited like sweet wheat.
units.literal: Emperor Hui, Yuankang 2, spring — bamboo on the borders of Baxi commandery flowered purple and bore fruit like wheat, with green outer skin, red-white inside, and a sweet taste.

units.zh: 元康九年六月庚子，有桑生東宮西廂，日長尺餘，甲辰枯死。
units.en: On gengzi in the sixth month of Yuankang 9, a mulberry shot up in the Eastern Palace’s west wing, grew more than a chi a day, and died on jiachen.
units.literal: Yuankang 9, sixth month, gengzi — a mulberry grew in the western wing of the Eastern Palace, lengthening more than a chi each day; on jiachen it withered and died.

units.zh: 此與殷太戊同妖，太子不能悟，故至廢戮也。
units.en: Like Shang precedent, the crown prince ignored the sign.
units.literal: This matches Yin emperor Taiwu's portent; the heir could not understand — hence deposition and slaughter.

units.zh: 班固稱「野木生朝而暴長，小人將暴居大臣之位，危國亡家之象，朝將為墟也。」
units.en: Ban Gu said: "Wild wood in court growing wildly means petty men will usurp ministers' seats — image of state ruin; the court will be waste."
units.literal: Ban Gu said: "Wild wood in court growing wildly means petty men will usurp ministers' seats — image of state ruin; the court will be waste."

units.zh: 是後孫秀、張林用事，遂至大亂。
units.en: Afterwards Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin took charge, leading to great disorder.
units.literal: Thereafter Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin held power until great chaos.

units.zh: 永康元年四月，立皇孫臧為皇太孫。
units.en: In the first year of Yongkang, Sima Zang became heir-apparent.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, fourth month — imperial grandson Zang was made heir.

units.zh: 五月甲子，就東宮，桑又生於西廂。
units.en: The mulberry returned when Zang entered.
units.literal: Fifth month jiazi — entering the Eastern Palace mulberry again grew in the west wing.

units.zh: 明年，趙王倫篡位，鴆殺臧，此與湣懷同妖也。
units.en: Lun's coup killed Zang like earlier heirs.
units.literal: Next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped and poisoned Zang — same portent as Min and Huai.

units.zh: 是月，壯武國有桑化為柏，而張華遇害。
units.en: Mulberry-cypress shift coincided with Zhang Hua's death.
units.literal: That month Zhuangwu princedom saw mulberry turn to cypress while Zhang Hua was murdered.

units.zh: 壯武，華之封邑也。
units.en: The omen struck his domain.
units.literal: Zhuangwu was Hua's fief.

units.zh: 孝懷帝永嘉二年冬，項縣桑樹有聲如解材，人謂之桑樹哭。
units.en: In the winter of Yongjia 2 under Emperor Huai, a Xiang county mulberry sounded like splitting wood, so people called it “the mulberry tree crying.”
units.literal: Emperor Huai, Yongjia 2, winter — a mulberry tree in Xiang county made a sound like timber being split; people called it “the mulberry tree crying.”

units.zh: 案劉向說，「桑者喪也」，又為哭聲，不祥之甚。
units.en: Liu Xiang said: "Mulberry sounds like mourning"; also weeping — utmost ill omen.
units.literal: Liu Xiang said: "Mulberry sounds like mourning"; also weeping — utmost ill omen.

units.zh: 是時京師虛弱，胡寇交侵，東海王越無衛國之心，四年冬季而南出，五年春薨於此城。
units.en: Sima Yue abandoned Luoyang and died on campaign.
units.literal: Then the capital was weak, Hu raiders crossed, Prince Donghai Yue had no mind to defend; winter of year four he marched south; spring five he died in that city.

units.zh: 石勒邀其眾，圍而射之，王公以下至眾庶，死者十餘萬人。
units.en: Shi Le massacred Yue's army.
units.literal: Shi Le ambushed his host, surrounded and shot them; from princes down to commoners over a hundred thousand died.

units.zh: 又剖越棺，焚其屍。
units.en: Le violated Yue's grave.
units.literal: They also opened Yue's coffin and burned his corpse.

units.zh: 是敗也，中原無所請命，洛京亦尋覆沒，桑哭之應也。
units.en: The fall of Jin answered the crying trees.
units.literal: That defeat left the central plain without refuge; Luoyang soon fell — answer to mulberry weeping.

units.zh: 六年五月，無錫縣有四株茱萸樹，相樛而生，狀若連理。
units.en: Dogwood trees fused in Wuxi.
units.literal: Sixth year fifth month — four cornus trees in Wuxi county intertwined like intertwined virtue.

units.zh: 先是，郭景純筮延陵蝘鼠，遇《臨》之《益》，曰：「後當復有妖樹生，若瑞而非，辛螫之木也，儻有此，東西數百里必有作逆者。」
units.en: Earlier Guo Pu divined Yanling mole-crickets, drew Lin changing to Yi, said: "Later an uncanny tree will grow — seeming auspicious yet not, a biting acrid wood; if so within several hundred li east-west a rebel will rise."
units.literal: Earlier Guo Pu divined Yanling mole-crickets, drew Lin changing to Yi, said: "Later an uncanny tree will grow — seeming auspicious yet not, a biting acrid wood; if so within several hundred li east-west a rebel will rise."

units.zh: 及此木生，其後徐馥果作亂，亦草妖也。
units.en: Xu Fu's rising matched the dogwood.
units.literal: When this tree appeared Xu Fu indeed rebelled — also grass portent.

units.zh: 郭又以為「木不曲直」。
units.en: Guo also classed it as "wood not straight or bent."
units.literal: Guo also classed it as "wood not straight or bent."

units.zh: 其七月，豫章郡有樟樹久枯，是月忽更榮茂，與漢昌邑枯社復生同占。
units.en: A dead camphor greened like Han portents.
units.literal: That seventh month a long-dead camphor in Yuzhang commandery suddenly flourished — same reading as Han Changyi's withered altar reviving.

units.zh: 是懷湣淪陷之征，元帝中興之應也。
units.en: It foretold lost north and southern revival.
units.literal: This augured Huai and Min's fall and Yuan-di's restoration.

units.zh: 明帝太寧元年九月，會稽剡縣木生如人面。
units.en: In the ninth month of Taining 1 under Emperor Ming, a tree in Shan county bore a human-face shape.
units.literal: Emperor Ming, Taining 1, ninth month — a tree in Shan county, Kuaiji, grew something like a human face.

units.zh: 是後王敦稱兵作逆，禍敗無成。
units.en: Wang Dun's revolt followed.
units.literal: Afterward Wang Dun mutinied and failed.

units.zh: 昔漢哀成之世並有此妖，而人貌備具，故春禍亦大。
units.en: Han precedents were graver.
units.literal: Han emperors Ai and Cheng had this too, yet faces were complete — hence great calamity.

units.zh: 今此但如人面而已，故其變也輕矣。
units.en: A partial face meant milder trouble.
units.literal: Now only a face — hence lighter change.

units.zh: 成帝五月癸亥，曲阿有柳樹枯倒六載，是日忽復起生，至九年五月甲戌，吳縣吳雄家有死榆樹，是日因風雨起生，與漢上林斷柳起生同象。
units.en: In Emperor Cheng's fifth month, on guihai, a willow at Qu'a that had lain withered for six years suddenly rose and lived again. In the fifth month of the ninth year, on jiaxu, a dead elm at Wu Xiong's house in Wu County likewise rose and lived again amid wind and rain, the same omen as the broken willow that revived in Han Shanglin Park.
units.literal: Emperor Cheng fifth month guihai — a willow in Qu'a dead six years suddenly revived; ninth year fifth month jiaxu a dead elm at Wu Xiong's home in Wu county revived in wind and rain — like Han Shanglin broken willow reviving.

units.zh: 初，康帝為吳王，于時雖改封琅邪，而猶食吳郡為邑，是帝越正體饗國之象也。
units.en: Emperor Kang, formerly Prince of Wu, still drew Wu commandery as his fief though moved to Langya — an image of his succeeding to the throne.
units.literal: At first Emperor Kang was Prince of Wu; though later enfeoffed Langya he still drew revenue from Wu commandery — omen that the true body would feast on the realm.

units.zh: 曲阿先亦吳地，象見吳邑雄之舍，又天意乎！
units.en: Qu'a too was once Wu land; that the omen appeared at Wu Xiong's residence in a Wu town — was that not also Heaven's will?
units.literal: Qu'a was once Wu land; the sign appeared at Wu Xiong's Wu home — was it not Heaven's will?

units.zh: 哀帝興寧三年五月癸卯，廬陵西昌縣修明家有僵栗樹，是日忽復起生。
units.en: On guimao in the fifth month of Xingning 3 under Emperor Ai, a dead chestnut tree at Xiu Ming’s house in Xichang revived.
units.literal: Emperor Ai, Xingning 3, fifth month, guimao — at Xiu Ming’s home in Xichang county, Luling, there was a withered chestnut tree; on this day it suddenly rose and lived again.

units.zh: 時孝武年始四歲，俄而哀帝崩，海西即位，未幾而廢，簡文越自籓王，入纂大業，登阼享國，又不逾二年，而孝武嗣統。
units.en: When Xiaowu was only four, Ai soon died, Haixi took the throne and was soon deposed, Jianwen crossed from a prince's fief to inherit the great enterprise and ruled less than two years, then Xiaowu succeeded.
units.literal: Then Xiaowu was only four; soon Ai died, Haixi took throne, soon deposed; Jianwen crossed from prince to inherit, ruled under two years, then Xiaowu succeeded.

units.zh: 帝諱昌明，識者竊謂西昌修明之祥，帝諱實應焉。
units.en: Place names echoed Sima Yao's taboo.
units.literal: The emperor's taboo name was Changming; augurs secretly said Xichang-Xiuming omens matched his name.

units.zh: 是亦與漢宣帝同象也。
units.en: Parallels were drawn to Liu Xun.
units.literal: This also echoed Han Xuandi's portent.

units.zh: 海西太和元年，涼州楊樹生松。
units.en: In Taihe 1 under the Duke of Haixi, Liangzhou poplars sprouted pine growth.
units.literal: Haixi, Taihe 1 — poplars in Liangzhou grew pines.

units.zh: 天戒若曰，松者不改柯易葉，楊者柔脆之木，今松生於楊，豈非永久之業將集危亡之地邪？
units.en: Hard pine on soft poplar mocked false permanence.
units.literal: Heaven warns: pine never changes bough or leaf; poplar is soft and brittle; pine growing on poplar — does not lasting enterprise gather where peril waits?

units.zh: 是時張天錫稱雄於涼州，尋而降苻堅。
units.en: Zhang Tianxi held sway in Liangzhou and soon surrendered to Fu Jian.
units.literal: Then Zhang Tianxi lorded Liangzhou, soon surrendered to Fu Jian.

units.zh: 孝武太元十四年六月，建甯郡銅樂縣枯樹斷折，忽然自立相屬。
units.en: In the sixth month of Taiyuan 14 under Emperor Xiaowu, a broken dead tree in Tongle, Jianning, stood itself upright and rejoined.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, Taiyuan 14, sixth month — in Tongle county, Jianning commandery, a dead tree had broken, then suddenly stood up by itself and joined together.

units.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「棄正作淫，厥妖木斷自屬。
units.en: Jing Fang says: "Abandon rectitude for debauchery — its portent: timber breaks yet joins itself.
units.literal: Jing Fang says: "Abandon rectitude for debauchery — its portent: timber breaks yet joins itself.

units.zh: 妃後有專，木僕反立。」
units.en: When consorts monopolize favor, fallen wood stands upright."
units.literal: When consorts monopolize favor, fallen wood stands upright."

units.zh: 是時正道多僻，其後張夫人專寵，及帝崩，兆庶歸咎張氏焉。
units.en: The omen was read against a crooked court: Lady Zhang later monopolized favor, and when the emperor died, common opinion blamed the Zhangs.
units.literal: At that time the right way was much perverted; later Lady Zhang monopolized favor, and when the emperor died, the multitudes blamed the Zhang clan.

units.zh: 安帝元興三年，荊、江二州界竹生實，如麥。
units.en: In Yuanxing 3 under Emperor An, bamboo between Jing and Jiang fruited like wheat.
units.literal: Emperor An, Yuanxing 3 — bamboo on the borders of Jing and Jiang provinces bore fruit like wheat.

units.zh: 義熙二年九月，揚武將軍營士陳蓋家有苦蕒菜，莖高四尺六寸，廣三尺二寸，厚三寸，亦草妖也。
units.en: In the ninth month of Yixi 2, a giant bitter herb grew in soldier Chen Gai’s barracks household, another grass portent.
units.literal: Yixi 2, ninth month — at the home of Chen Gai, a soldier in the Yangwu general’s camp, there was a bitter herb whose stem was four chi six cun high, three chi two cun broad, and three cun thick; this too was a grass portent.

units.zh: 此殆與吳終同象。
units.en: It echoed Wu's final omens.
units.literal: This nearly matches Wu's end.

units.zh: 識者以為苦蕒者，買勤苦也。
units.en: Kǔ mǎi punned on purchased toil.
units.literal: Readers thought bitter greens meant buying bitterness.

units.zh: 自後歲歲征討，百姓勞苦，是買苦也。
units.en: Endless war bought national suffering.
units.literal: Thereafter year on year campaigned — the people bought bitterness.

units.zh: 十餘年中，姚泓滅，兵始戢，是苦蕒之應也。
units.en: Yao Hong's fall ended the campaigns.
units.literal: Within a dozen years Yao Hong was destroyed and arms finally rested — answer of the bitter greens.

units.zh: 義熙中，宮城上及御道左右皆生蒺藜，亦草妖也。
units.en: Jiankang's walls sprouted caltrops.
units.literal: Yixi years — thorns grew on palace walls and along the imperial ways — also grass portent.

units.zh: 蒺藜有刺，不可踐而行。
units.en: Caltrops barred the avenues.
units.literal: Thorns have spikes — you cannot walk them.

units.zh: 生宮牆及馳道，天戒若曰，人君不聽政，雖有宮室馳道，若空廢也，故生蒺藜。
units.en: Heaven turned avenues into brambles for an idle throne.
units.literal: Growing on palace wall and carriage road, Heaven warns: the ruler neglects government — though halls and highways exist they are void — hence thorns.

units.zh: （分段）
units.en: Divider.
units.literal: (Sectional marker.)

units.zh: 羽蟲之孽
units.en: Subsection: avian omens.
units.literal: Calamities from feathered insects.

units.zh: （分段）
units.en: Divider.
units.literal: (Sectional marker.)

units.zh: 魏文帝黃初四年五月，有鵜鶘鳥集靈芝池。
units.en: In the fifth month of Huangchu 4 under Wei Emperor Wen, pelicans gathered at Lingzhi Pool.
units.literal: Wei Emperor Wen, Huangchu 4, fifth month — pelicans gathered at Lingzhi Pool.

units.zh: 案劉向說，此羽蟲之孽，又青祥也。
units.en: Liu Xiang filed pelicans under green portents.
units.literal: Liu Xiang's doctrine: feathered insect calamity, also green omen.

units.zh: 詔曰：「此詩人所謂汙澤者也。
units.en: An edict said: "This is what poets call the fouled marsh.
units.literal: An edict said: "This is what poets call the fouled marsh.

units.zh: 《曹詩》『刺共公遠君子近小人』，今豈有賢智之士處於下位，否則斯鳥何為而至哉！
units.en: The Cao ode "rebukes Duke Gong for shunning gentlemen and cherishing petty men" — are wise men now stuck in low posts, else why would this bird come?
units.literal: The Cao ode "rebukes Duke Gong for shunning gentlemen and cherishing petty men" — are wise men now stuck in low posts, else why would this bird come?

units.zh: 其博舉天下俊德茂才獨行君子，以答曹人之刺。」
units.en: Let all recommend outstanding talent, solitary integrity, and gentlemen — answering the Cao people's satire."
units.literal: Let all recommend outstanding talent, solitary integrity, and gentlemen — answering the Cao people's satire."

units.zh: 於是楊彪、管寧之徒咸見薦舉，些所謂睹妖知懼者也。
units.en: Notables were nominated in response.
units.literal: Thereupon Yang Biao, Guan Ning, and such were recommended — this is seeing portent and fearing.
